extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and sustaining distinct character voices in fiction—how to shape dialogue and internal voice using background, personality, genre conventions, emotional state, and arc-driven change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct character voices deepen character development
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct character voices deepen character development by highlighting personal histories and motivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post emphasizes that unique voices make characters relatable and memorable, connecting readers more deeply with the narrative and bringing the story to life. Use voice to reveal backstory and motivation rather than exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique voices create conflict and tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Differing voices can lead to misunderstandings and conflict, propelling the plot forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat voice differences as a story tool: let clashing speech patterns, beliefs, or registers generate friction that advances scenes and character arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key elements that shape character voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Background, personality, emotional state, and environment contribute to a character's unique voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: upbringing, culture, and education influence speech. Personality: traits such as humor, sarcasm, or seriousness are reflected in dialogue. Emotional state: urgency or subdued tone changes voice in-scene. Environment: regional dialects, colloquialisms, and setting inform expression. Consider all these factors together when crafting speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain voice consistency throughout character arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice consistency is crucial for believable character development; even as voice evolves, core speech patterns should be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that changes in a character's speech are motivated and gradual; retain identifiable rhythms, vocabulary preferences, or tics so the character remains recognizable across the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray voice evolution over time
rubrics_metrics.description: A character's voice can and should change to reflect personal growth, challenges, and maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include gradual shifts in vocabulary and tone, alterations in dialogue structure, and adjustments to catchphrases or speech patterns. Use these shifts to show development while avoiding abrupt, unmotivated changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align voice with genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Character voices should reflect genre-specific expectations to enhance immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: fantasy uses rich, ornate language; science fiction uses technical jargon and futuristic slang; literary fiction favors reflective, introspective dialogue; thrillers use short, punchy sentences. Adapt register, diction, and cadence to fit genre norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use narrative techniques beyond dialogue to convey voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal monologue and narrative voice supplement dialogue to convey a character's perspective and deepen voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ free indirect discourse, interior thought, and descriptive choices that echo a character's speech patterns to create a unified voice across narration and dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical exercise: keep a voice journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing conversations or monologues in a character's voice helps solidify speech patterns and emotional nuances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author recommends a 'voice journal' to discover and maintain consistent tics, rhythms, and vocabulary. It can reveal new facets of the character and make it easier to keep voice consistent in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshopping and feedback to refine voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer feedback and mentorship help identify weak or indistinct voices and refine character speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in workshops (e.g., the author's courses) to get hands-on critique; outside readers can point out when characters sound too similar or when voice shifts feel unearned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dialogue to reveal background, emotion, and motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-crafted dialogue should reveal a character's history, emotional state, and goals rather than only convey plot information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with speaking styles and subtext—what a character chooses not to say or how they phrase something can communicate as much as explicit content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft conversations to highlight distinct voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Memorable character conversations arise when each participant speaks with a consistent, recognizably different voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design exchanges so that contrast in diction, pacing, and tone reveals relationships and moves the plot; avoid homogenized dialogue where multiple characters sound the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polished prose: tightness and word choice
rubrics_metrics.description: In revision, ensure every word serves a purpose; eliminate unnecessary adjectives and adverbs and prefer strong verbs and precise nouns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tightening prose not only strengthens overall writing but clarifies voice—lean sentences help distinctive speech patterns stand out. Ask during revision whether each word advances character voice or scene.
